topic.title: the next room
topic.claim: Papa never tells you he's proud. He tells the neighbour, loudly, while you're in the next room.
topic.moment: You're inside and you hear papa through the wall, telling Sharma uncle exactly what you earn and where you work.

turn.believed: Papa doesn't say he's proud because he isn't the type, or isn't quite proud.
turn.actually: He's proud enough to broadcast it to the whole lane, just never to your face.

topic.because: Praising you directly might soften you, or break a lifetime of a certain kind of distance. The neighbour is how he says it where you can hear but he doesn't have to look at you.
topic.payoff: He wasn't hiding that he's proud. He was performing it, loud enough for you to overhear.
topic.feeling: the warmth of being loved sideways
topic.villain: the arrangement where a father's pride has to travel through a neighbour to reach his child
topic.behaviour: fathers brag about their kids to everyone except the kid
topic.mechanism: saying it to your face breaks the distance he's used to, so he routes the pride through someone you can overhear
topic.send_to: a friend whose dad has never once said it to them directly
topic.why_now: home visits this season when you overhear these conversations again

_ledger.text:
[cover] Papa tells the neighbour he's proud. [Never you.]
You hear it through the wall, and it still counts.
 

[slide 1] Papa tells the neighbour he's proud. Never you.
Swipe to read →

[slide 2] You're home for a few days. Sunday morning, the pressure cooker hissing, the fan on low.
Through the wall you hear papa on the balcony with Sharma uncle. He's listing your salary, your company, where you work now.

[slide 3] He has never said any of it to your face. Not once.
You settled this years ago. Some fathers say it, yours just isn't the type.

[slide 4] But the balcony door is open. It's always open when this happens. And he's saying it a notch louder than the chat needs.
The volume is a choice.

[slide 5] Saying it to your face means looking at you while he does it. That breaks a distance he's kept since you can remember.
The neighbour is easier. You still catch every word.

[slide 6] He wasn't hiding that he's proud of you.
He was performing it, at full volume, for an audience of one in the next room.

[end card] Open this the next time you're home and hear him on the phone about you.
Send to your sibling whose dad has never once said it to their face either.

[caption] Some fathers can only say it loudly, to someone else, while you pretend not to hear.

[alt text] A six-slide carousel. A grown child is home for the weekend and overhears their father on the balcony bragging about their job and salary to a neighbour, though he has never said he is proud to their face. The post reframes this: the father isn't hiding his pride, he's performing it loud enough for the child in the next room to overhear.
